answer: At 12/31/2024, Allstate had $500 million of Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures. The scheduled maturity is May 15, 2057, and the final maturity is May 15, 2067. They are redeemable at par plus accrued interest on or after May 15, 2037. Earlier redemption in certain circumstances is at par or a make-whole price, whichever is greater. Interest is 6.500% fixed, paid semi-annually, to May 15, 2037. After that it is paid quarterly at three-month CME Term SOFR plus 0.26161% plus 2.120%. Interest can be deferred for up to 10 years and compounds during deferral. While interest is deferred, dividends and buybacks on common and preferred stock are restricted. The company has reserved 75 million common shares to satisfy its obligation to issue stock in certain circumstances if interest is deferred. A replacement capital covenant runs to 2067 and restricts repayment or redemption without qualifying capital raises, subject to exceptions.

answer: Yes. Workday reports a gross revenue retention rate, about 98% as of January 31, 2025. It is defined as the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers. It compares the ARR of customers at the prior period-end with ARR from that same set of customers at the current period-end. It counts losses from product or customer churn but excludes add-ons and net expansions (volume and price adjustments). ARR is the annualized value of active subscription contracts: total contract value divided by days in the term, times 365. It is constant-currency, non-GAAP, and excludes certain contracts such as short-term implementation and testing tenants. No net retention metric appears in the 10-K.

answer: The 10-Q gives these terms. On March 7, 2025, KKR issued 51,750,000 shares of 6.25% Series D Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock, a $2.59 billion aggregate liquidation preference and about $2.54 billion of net proceeds. The liquidation preference is $50.00 per share plus accumulated and unpaid dividends. Dividends are cumulative at 6.25% a year, paid in cash, common stock or a mix, quarterly on Mar 1, Jun 1, Sep 1 and Dec 1 from June 1, 2025 through March 1, 2028. The shares convert automatically on about March 1, 2028 into 0.3312–0.4140 common shares each, based on a 20-trading-day VWAP. No dividends or repurchases of junior stock are allowed unless accumulated Series D dividends are paid or set aside. The 10-Q does not state the Series D voting rights, the purpose of the offering, or an offering price other than the $50 liquidation preference, so those cannot be determined from this filing.

Aryeo (Jul 2023, ~$35M), Spruce (Sep 2023, ~$19M cash) and Follow Up Boss (Dec 2023, $484M including $81M contingent consideration) were followed by Virtual Staging AI (Oct 2024, terms not given in the excerpts I read). VRX Media (Dec 2022) is also named. The strategy is an "integrated software experience" for agents and buyers/sellers, plus transaction capability through Spruce's title and escrow platform. So the deals support the agent-software and transaction-workflow side of the mix. The mix shift toward Mortgages and Rentals comes mainly from organic growth, and the filing does not quantify acquired revenue.

answer: At December 31, 2024, Allstate had $500 million outstanding of Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures. They have a scheduled maturity of May 15, 2057 and a final maturity of May 15, 2067. They are redeemable at par plus accrued interest on or after May 15, 2037, or earlier at par or a make-whole price in certain circumstances. Interest is 6.500% fixed, paid semi-annually, until May 15, 2037. After that it is paid quarterly at three-month CME Term SOFR plus 2.120% plus a 0.26161% spread adjustment (replacing LIBOR). Interest can be deferred for up to 10 years, with compounding. During deferral, dividends and stock repurchases are restricted. Allstate may also have to issue stock, and it has reserved 75 million shares for that. A replacement capital covenant limits repayment or redemption on or before May 15, 2067, and it terminates in 2067.

They have a scheduled maturity of May 15, 2057 and a final maturity of May 15, 2067. They are redeemable at par plus accrued interest on or after May 15, 2037, or earlier at a make-whole price in certain circumstances. Interest is fixed at 6.500%, paid semi-annually, until May 15, 2037. After that it is paid quarterly at three-month CME Term SOFR plus 2.120% plus a 0.26161% spread adjustment. Allstate may defer interest for up to 10 years, with compounding. During deferral it cannot pay dividends on common or preferred stock, and it has reserved 75 million shares to cover its obligation to issue stock to pay deferred interest. A replacement capital covenant runs to 2067.

answer: In Item 1A, under "Risks Related to Legal and Regulatory Matters", Paylocity lists five regulatory and legal risks. (1) Changing regulation of its software and services, including tax, benefit, wage-and-hour and employment laws and money transmitter/money services business licensing. This could raise costs, delay products and bring fines if it were deemed an unlicensed money transmitter. (2) Regulation of AI and machine learning, including US and EU legislation and the resulting scrutiny, litigation and fines. (3) Data privacy laws (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA and others), with fines up to 4% of worldwide revenue under GDPR, rising enforcement and reputational harm. (4) Adverse tax laws, including state sales and use tax exposure for past periods. (5) Costly litigation that insurance may not cover. Elsewhere it also flags regulatory fines after security incidents, rising cybersecurity compliance costs, errors in tax and regulatory filings, and regulatory risks of international expansion.

answer: As of December 31, 2024, Allstate had $500 million of Series A 6.500% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Junior Subordinated Debentures outstanding. They have a scheduled maturity of May 15, 2057 and a final maturity of May 15, 2067. They are redeemable at par on or after May 15, 2037, or earlier at par or a make-whole price in certain circumstances. Interest is 6.500% fixed, paid semi-annually, until May 15, 2037. After that it is paid quarterly at three-month LIBOR (replaced by CME Term SOFR) plus 2.120%, with a 0.26161% spread adjustment. Allstate may defer interest for up to 10 years. While interest is deferred, it cannot pay dividends on common or preferred stock. It has reserved 75 million common shares for the deferral feature. A replacement capital covenant, benefiting holders of the $800 million Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2053, restricts repayment or redemption through 2067.

answer: KKR issued 51,750,000 shares of 6.25% Series D Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock on March 7, 2025, for about $2.59 billion aggregate liquidation preference (net proceeds $2,543.4 million). The liquidation preference is $50.00 per share plus accumulated and unpaid dividends. answer: Yes, Workday reports a gross revenue retention rate (approximately 98% as of January 31, 2025). It is defined as the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers: ARR from the same set of customers at current period-end divided by their ARR at the prior period-end. It reflects losses from product or customer churn and excludes add-ons and net expansions (volume and price adjustments). ARR is the annualized value of active subscription contracts (total contract value ÷ days in term × 365), on a constant-currency basis, excluding certain short-term non-core contracts. No net retention metric is reported in this 10-K.
